-79.91783,43.26394.name: McMaster University
-79.91783,43.26394.status: Certificate of GAP Last visit: interim, February 2024
-79.91783,43.26394.desc: An institution certified by the Canadian Council on Animal Care for its use of animals in science. Certificate of GAP Last visit: interim, February 2024. CCAC certification is a condition of federal research funding rather than a licence, so an institution outside it is not necessarily outside the work — it may simply not take federal money. The CCAC publishes names and certificate status and no addresses, so this point marks the institution rather than the building where animals are held.

-71.04000,42.34800.name: Ginkgo Bioworks — biosecurity
-71.04000,42.34800.desc: The biosecurity arm of a large synthetic-biology company, running pathogen monitoring at airports and in wastewater under government contract. A private firm holding both the capacity to design organisms and the contract to detect them is a concentration worth seeing on one map.

6.14000,46.23200.name: WHO — antimicrobial resistance surveillance
6.14000,46.23200.desc: Tracks resistant infections, now associated with over a million deaths a year. Resistance is what makes engineered alternatives — phages, engineered probiotics, novel antibiotics from engineered microbes — fundable at all, and it is also driven by antibiotic use in engineered-feed livestock systems. The same industry is on both sides of the problem.

6.14000,46.23200.name: WHO Laboratory Biosafety Manual
6.14000,46.23200.desc: The reference that defines what containment levels mean. Its fourth edition moved from prescribing equipment by pathogen to requiring a risk assessment for the work actually being done — which is more flexible and puts more weight on the judgement of the institution doing it. There is no definition of BSL3+ in it, or anywhere else, which is why that category is self-declared.

6.14000,46.23200.name: WHO — variola virus repository inspections
6.14000,46.23200.desc: Smallpox exists in two declared laboratories, one in the United States and one in Russia, and the WHO inspects both every two years. They are the only laboratories anywhere subject to international inspection of this kind, agreed because the virus was eradicated and the stocks kept deliberately. Every other maximum-containment facility on Earth is inspected by its own government or by nobody — which makes two laboratories the exception that shows the shape of the rule.

-77.21300,39.14400.name: GeneDx
-77.21300,39.14400.desc: Sequences exomes and genomes at scale for rare disease diagnosis, largely in children. Rare disease is where sequencing has the clearest benefit and the least argument attached, and it is also how a very large paediatric genomic database gets assembled.

7.49510,9.05790.name: National Biotechnology Research and Development Agency (NBRDA)
7.49510,9.05790.desc: Nigeria's biotechnology development agency, which sets national biotechnology policy and runs the confined field trials that later become applications to the biosafety agency. It also hosts the Nigerian chapter of the Open Forum on Agricultural Biotechnology, an outreach programme funded from outside the country. Development, trials and public persuasion sit in one agency; the approval sits in another. Reading the two together is how you see whether the separation is real.

78.48670,17.38500.name: Indian Immunologicals Limited
78.48670,17.38500.state: Hyderabad — a subsidiary of the National Dairy Development Board
78.48670,17.38500.desc: One of India's largest veterinary vaccine producers, holding roughly a fifth of that national market, and owned by the National Dairy Development Board rather than by private shareholders. It has also worked on human vaccines built by codon de-optimisation — rewriting a virus's genetic code so it replicates poorly while still provoking immunity, which is genetic engineering of a pathogen by any definition, undertaken in a research collaboration with an Australian university. It belongs in this facet because the vaccine industry outside the United States and Europe is largely absent from this map, and because a state-linked producer answers to a different set of pressures than a listed animal health company: its output is priced for a dairy sector rather than for a shareholder.

78.48670,17.38500.name: Nuziveedu Seeds
78.48670,17.38500.desc: India's largest domestic seed company, founded in 1973, and the licensee that fought its licensor to a standstill. It took a Bt cotton licence from the Monsanto joint venture in 2004 for an initial ten years, on a recurring trait-value payment; when state governments began capping seed prices and the licensor would not reduce the fee, the Indian companies stopped paying, the licence was terminated, and litigation ran from 2015 to a settlement in March 2021, passing through the Delhi High Court twice, an arbitration and the Supreme Court. Alongside it the agriculture ministry set a national price for engineered cotton seed and the royalty allowed on it, and asked the competition authority to investigate the licensor. Its chairman was simultaneously president of the national seed association — the same person leading the company, the trade body and the public argument. This is the clearest case on the map of a licensee with enough domestic weight to change the terms of a trait licence rather than accept them.
